name: Blue Tory
summary: Blue Toryism is the market-oriented, fiscally conservative wing of Canadian conservatism, favouring lower taxes, smaller and cheaper government, privatisation, deregulation and free trade. Its adherents emphasise individual self-reliance and personal responsibility rather than the communitarian state activism of Red Toryism, and are not necessarily socially conservative.
scope: The Canadian usage of the term: the free-enterprise, small-government strand represented by Preston Manning's Reform Party, Mike Harris, Ralph Klein, Stephen Harper and Pierre Poilievre, as described in Wikipedia and the Canadian Encyclopedia. Official positions are read from the Conservative Party of Canada Policy Declaration, a big-tent document, so social-policy answers are lower confidence. The British informal use of the term and the Red Tory tradition are excluded.

keyFigures.name: Stephen Harper
keyFigures.role: Prime Minister 2006-2015 whose government cut the GST and corporate taxes, named by Wikipedia as a Blue Tory.

keyFigures.name: Mike Harris
keyFigures.role: Premier of Ontario 1995-2002, who cut income taxes and spending, named by Wikipedia as a Blue Tory.

keyFigures.name: Preston Manning
keyFigures.role: Founder of the Reform Party, which sought a radical reduction of state responsibilities.

sources.title: Conservatism
sources.author: The Canadian Encyclopedia
sources.usedFor: Market camp's lower taxes, deregulation and privatisation; Reform's devolution to provinces; Mulroney free trade.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The CPC declaration backs reasonable access to quality healthcare regardless of ability to pay, and Harper-era Blue Tories kept the public system while favouring provincial delivery; Harris-style cuts show reluctance on expansion.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Blue Tories prioritise job creation and low payroll and business costs, and see substantial wage-floor increases as a cost to employers; wage setting is also largely provincial.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The declaration names a free competitive economy as the best guarantor of prosperity, and Blue Toryism is defined by free-enterprise orientation.

public-ownership.rationale: The Wikipedia article lists privatisation (e.g. the Wheat Board) among Blue Tory policies and the declaration limits government to tasks the private sector cannot do more efficiently.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The declaration seeks broad-based tax relief, a less progressive system with fewer brackets and lower capital gains tax.

unions-good.rationale: Blue Tories are wary of union power; the declaration's section on workers stresses freedom from compulsory membership as a condition of employment, and Harris and Klein confronted public-sector unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: The declaration lists the right to own property as a founding principle and urges a constitutional property-rights amendment with compensation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deregulation is part of the market camp's programme as described by the Canadian Encyclopedia, and the declaration favours reduced government interference in the economy.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Wikipedia article notes Harris-era cuts to welfare and the declaration says individuals must provide for themselves, though it accepts help for those in need.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership conflicts with the free-enterprise and private-property principles; no Blue Tory source endorses it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The declaration mentions both security and privacy of the individual, and Blue Tories split between security hawks and libertarians.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The CPC declaration opposes decriminalising illicit drugs and taxpayer-funded safe supply, though libertarian-leaning Blue Tories dissent.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The declaration commits to protect freedom of expression, including on campuses, and opposes compelled speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The declaration stresses Parliament, ministerial accountability and free votes; a leader bypassing gridlock runs against a limited-government, constitutional stance.

state-harmful.rationale: Blue Tories want limited government rather than none: the declaration gives the state roles in protecting life, property, borders and infrastructure.

limit-guns.rationale: The declaration recognises the legitimacy of private firearm ownership and promises to resist pressure to the contrary, favouring targeting criminals rather than strict limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: The declaration backs a well-armed military and tougher enforcement, mandatory minimums and more officers on the streets.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources do not address it; Blue Tory personal-freedom leanings pull one way and the party's tough-on-crime and family-values base the other, with the latter dominant in Harper-era policy.

decide-locally.rationale: The declaration favours strong provincial governments and limits on the federal spending power; Reform called for transferring powers from Ottawa to the provinces.

rehabilitation.rationale: The declaration emphasises mandatory minimum sentences and bail restrictions over rehabilitation, though it also mentions training for inmates.

traditional-family.rationale: The declaration supports tax fairness for families including stay-at-home parents; Blue Tories stress self-reliance but social conservatism is not required of them.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The declaration treats the definition of marriage as a matter of conscience with free votes, and Blue Tories are not necessarily social conservatives.

abortion-legal.rationale: The declaration lists abortion as a conscience issue with free votes; Blue Tories as a group are split and libertarian-minded members lean towards choice.

more-religion-public.rationale: Blue Tories emphasise personal freedom and are not necessarily socially conservative; the declaration favours freedom of worship and one law for all rather than a larger public religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The declaration stresses equality of all Canadians and the Charter's individual equality rights over group-based remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from the party's family-oriented, culturally conservative base, though Blue Tories' individualism makes this weak.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The declaration speaks of promoting Canada's history and traditions and honouring those who serve.

gradual-change.rationale: The Tory tradition, as the Encyclopedia describes it, values institutions such as Parliament and the monarchy, favouring prudent reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The declaration calls for a welcoming, well-managed system favouring skilled immigrants and a stronger economy; reductions are not a stated aim.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Harper-era Blue Toryism emphasised national sovereignty and the declaration speaks of obligations among nations without endorsing stronger supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: The declaration calls for reducing trade barriers and says free trade principles should apply to all sectors, and the Canadian Encyclopedia notes Mulroney's free trade deal.

nation-first.rationale: The declaration accepts obligations among nations while defending Canadian jurisdiction; Blue Tories are internationalist on trade but sovereigntist on other matters.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The sources I opened give no view on intervention abroad; Blue Tories are pro-alliance but wary of foreign adventures, so adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: The declaration commits to secure borders and a well-managed immigration system, which excludes eventually open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The declaration sees prosperity coming from a free competitive economy and opposes federal carbon pricing; growth limits contradict this.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The declaration opposes any federally imposed carbon tax or cap-and-trade system, and Blue Tories oppose drastic state-led climate measures.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources have no stated view; market optimism points to agreement while Tory prudence counsels caution.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The declaration supports the application of nuclear energy and its associated industries.

revolution-justified.rationale: Blue Tories value constitutional monarchy, Parliament and the democratic process, as the declaration states.

experts-over-public.rationale: Blue Tories are populist-leaning against elites and bureaucracy; no source addresses this directly.

central-planning.rationale: The declaration rests on a free competitive market economy and states its distrust of state economic direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: Blue Tories favour private ownership of enterprise, as the declaration and Wikipedia show, so public or worker ownership as the condition for markets is rejected.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed; the declaration favours simplified, lower taxes and strong private property, making a replacement land tax unlikely.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The declaration wants the right to enjoy the fruits of one's labour and less progressive taxation, and Canada has no inheritance tax that conservatives seek to add.

basic-income.rationale: The declaration stresses individual responsibility and work incentives; an unconditional income is generally opposed by Blue Tories, though some market conservatives accept variants.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The declaration seeks reduction of tariffs and trade barriers; protectionism is associated with the Macdonald-era Red Tory tradition the Wikipedia article contrasts with Blue Toryism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial planning conflicts with the free-enterprise orientation; the Wikipedia article contrasts Blue Toryism with Macdonald's interventionist National Policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Blue Tories support broad property ownership but not state intervention to spread it, and favour private enterprise at every scale.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rejected by the free competitive economy and property principles of the declaration.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream Blue Tories accept the Bank of Canada, though libertarian-leaning members may sympathise.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bargaining bodies conflict with free competitive markets and the limited-government principle.

one-party-rule.rationale: The declaration endorses Parliament, free votes and the democratic process.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The declaration's founding principles state a belief in Canada's constitutional monarchy, which a Blue Tory party member accepts as head of state.

democracy-best.rationale: The declaration affirms parliamentary democracy; the qualifier about bad voter choices is less discussed.

direct-votes.rationale: Reform populism backed referendums, and the declaration requires a referendum before electoral reform, but it keeps representative government generally.

workers-councils.rationale: Incompatible with the declaration's commitment to Parliament and a free-market economy.

right-to-secede.rationale: The declaration affirms federalism and the constitutional boundaries between governments, with no right of secession stated.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration affirms equality of all Canadians, though Tory tradition accepts hierarchy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed directly; constitutional order and rule of law imply opposition.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing in the sources glorifies war; the declaration honours those who serve but frames defence as deterrence, so this is inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The declaration backs freedom of worship and an Office of Religious Freedom but also one law for all; adherents split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The declaration rejects religious courts and affirms one law for all Canadians.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The declaration makes protecting citizens and borders a core government role and wants a well-armed national military.

military-superiority.rationale: The declaration supports a well-armed military and collective defence, but sets no aim of superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The declaration stresses equality of all Canadians and a welcoming immigration policy.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Blue Tories reject Marxist class analysis in favour of individual initiative.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The declaration limits government to ensuring equality of opportunity (Role of Government, ii).

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The declaration says Indigenous rights must be conferred within the Constitution and the Charter with equal individual rights, and stresses property rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the emphasis on fiscal restraint and individual rather than inherited responsibility.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the declaration's stress on Canadian jurisdiction and a federal nation-state rather than civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The declaration speaks of citizens' freedom to pursue their enlightened and legitimate self-interest within a free competitive economy.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The declaration places freedom of the individual first, though it also stresses personal responsibility.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The declaration treats the environment as a heritage to protect for future generations, framed in terms of human stewardship rather than intrinsic value.

limit-population.rationale: Active population limitation is not part of any Blue Tory source and clashes with the personal-freedom stance.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A worldview that credits enterprise, growth and resource development with prosperity (as in the declaration's energy and economy sections) rejects this verdict.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pro-market, but Tory caution about disruption to institutions; not addressed in sources.

human-enhancement.rationale: Libertarian leanings favour freedom while social conservatives oppose; no source addresses it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on accountable Parliamentary government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources are silent; privacy concerns and security-state instincts both exist among Blue Tories, so adherents are split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Blue Tories are market modernisers more than restorationists, in contrast to social conservatives.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Blue Tories claim common-sense pragmatism (Common Sense Revolution) but are ideologically committed to free markets.

direct-action.rationale: The declaration commits the party to Parliament and the democratic process, so change through direct action instead of elections is rejected.

means-match-ends.rationale: This is an anarchist question of method that the sources never address, and Blue Tories have no settled view on it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A return to hunter-gatherer life contradicts the declaration's aim of prosperity through a free competitive economy; inferred as the position is never discussed.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Specialisation and exchange in a competitive market economy are basic to the declaration's economic outlook, so abolishing the division of labour is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The declaration holds that individuals should enjoy the fruits of their labour to the greatest extent.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for profit in a free competitive economy is the model the declaration endorses.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Free-enterprise orientation treats profit as legitimate reward, not exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts the declaration's commitment to Parliament, free votes and constitutional democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: Compulsory collective farming conflicts with the declaration's property rights and its commitment that landowners keep control of their land.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a Blue Tory view; the declaration says global free trade is the best path to social and economic goals.

taxation-theft.rationale: Blue Tories want lower taxes but accept legitimate taxation to fund core government roles; the libertarian extreme is not the mainstream.

harm-principle.rationale: Libertarian-leaning personal-freedom views support it, though the party's stand on drugs conflicts, so this is inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The declaration emphasises individual rights and equality rights under the Charter over collective rights.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration supports a professional well-armed military and individual freedom.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Blue Tories value democratic accountability through Parliament and free votes more than emigration as the main check; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Blue Tories stress fiscal prudence, efficiency and Common Sense-style cost control in government.

positive-liberty.rationale: The declaration defines freedom as individual liberty to enjoy the fruits of one's labour, and provides equality of opportunity only.

media-academia-power.rationale: Conservative critique of media and universities exists; the declaration has free-speech-on-campus provisions.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians; mainstream parties disown it.

organic-representation.rationale: Declaration endorses Parliament and individual voting rather than corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Direction of every area of life by the state is the opposite of the declaration's principle that government should be limited to what individuals cannot do themselves.

national-rebirth.rationale: A radical national rebirth is not a Blue Tory theme; the declaration and Wikipedia describe incremental tax and spending reform instead.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The declaration supports defence of existing territory and international obligations.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on personal oaths conflicts with the declaration's parliamentary and constitutional government.

bound-labor.rationale: Legal bonding of labourers to land contradicts the freedom of individuals to enjoy the fruits of their labour in the declaration.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Blue Tories resist postmodern critiques; the declaration champions free speech and campus inquiry.

universal-morality.rationale: The declaration speaks of the value and dignity of all human life, but sources do not take a metaethical position.

single-common-good.rationale: Blue Tories emphasise individual pursuit of interests over a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not covered in the sources I opened; inferred from the Conservative Party's generally pro-Israel stance.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources do not address diaspora return rights, and nothing in Blue Tory principles settles the question.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration treats English and French as equal official languages.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Democratic votes by workers and the public over company decisions conflict with private property and the free enterprise orientation.

school-vouchers.rationale: Blue Tories favour market choice in public services, and the declaration says government should deliver only what private providers cannot do better.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Opposing deficit spending is a defining Blue Tory trait, and the declaration calls for fiscal prudence.

economic-freedom.rationale: The declaration ties prosperity and liberty to a free competitive economy and property rights.

rule-by-example.rationale: The declaration relies on parliamentary law and accountable ministers, not rulers' moral example, though it also asks for ethical conduct.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not directly addressed; Blue Tories assume the nation-state framework, as the declaration speaks of Canada as a nation state.

force-without-un.rationale: Blue Tory Harper-era positions leaned to alliance-based action; not stated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The declaration affirms freedom of worship; many Blue Tories hold religious conviction.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources do not address welfare eligibility for immigrants; Blue Tories want welfare limited but this specific restriction is not documented.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The declaration says individuals are responsible for providing for themselves, which supports work requirements for the able-bodied.

class-collaboration.rationale: The declaration treats prosperity as the result of enterprise and says the state should foster conditions where private initiative thrives, implying cooperation over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Sacrificing inherited institutions conflicts with the declaration's pledge to promote Canada's history and traditions.

dominated-front.rationale: Alliances of dominated nations against Western powers are alien to a party that backs collective defence with Western allies.

workers-nation.rationale: Class-based national organisation is alien to Blue Toryism, which speaks of individuals and taxpayers rather than classes.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The declaration affirms the equality of all Canadians, which weighs against laws prescribing distinct public roles for men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: Prohibiting interest conflicts with the declaration's commitment to a free competitive economy and capital markets.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The declaration's founding principles state a belief in the equality of all Canadians, which excludes legal racial classification.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Blue Toryism treats the state as limited and accountable to voters, not as a class instrument; the Marxist theory is rejected.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The declaration supports development of oil, gas and coal energy resources; Blue Tories from Alberta champion the energy sector.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The declaration seeks a welcoming system and integration of immigrants but does not demand abandoning original cultures; adherents differ.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy views contradict the declaration's welcoming immigration policy.

proportional-representation.rationale: The declaration requires a national referendum before any electoral reform, signalling reluctance to adopt proportional representation.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading one's government abroad is not a Blue Tory theme; the declaration speaks of accepting obligations among nations.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The declaration stresses equal opportunity for individuals, not structural diagnoses.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Reform populism and Poilievre-era rhetoric attacked elites, while the declaration pushes accountability.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Discouraging reproduction by state policy contradicts individual freedom and the declaration's belief in the dignity of all human life.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The sources do not address legal accountability for past abuses by security forces; no Blue Tory position is documented.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Blue Tories want limited but not minimal government; the declaration allows infrastructure and assistance roles.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Discouraging marriage across racial lines contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians and freedom of the individual.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The founding principles state a belief in the value and dignity of all human life and the equality of all Canadians.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is a Marxist debate Blue Tories do not engage; socialism itself is rejected in favour of a free economy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Blue Tories generally resist framing Canada as an illegitimate settler state, an inference.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The declaration rejects religious courts and says one law for all Canadians.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The declaration lists freedom of worship among founding principles and supports an Office of Religious Freedom.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Against agricultural industry and freedom; supply-managed cattle sectors exist.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: School curriculum is provincial and the sources do not address religious instruction; adherents split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory of the state that Blue Tories reject in favour of a limited government.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The declaration affirms democratic process and accountability to the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Free-trade orientation views trade as mutually beneficial, not a surplus contest.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced or pressured relocation of minorities contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians and individual freedom.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian axiom; mainstream Blue Tories accept state coercion for law enforcement.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition in the economy is endorsed; biological struggle between peoples is not.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Free speech and association commitments in the declaration weigh against party bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of liberty not addressed in the sources, and not a framing Blue Tories use.

separated-powers.rationale: The declaration affirms federalism, Parliament and judicial appointments process.

vanguard-party.rationale: A revolutionary vanguard contradicts the declaration's commitment to Parliament and the democratic process.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The declaration limits government to equal opportunity and compassion for those requiring assistance.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Property-owning democracy appeals to market conservatives; not a Canadian issue and not in sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The declaration's section on workers stresses protection from compelled union membership, which fits support for restrictions such as secret ballots.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not discussed; Blue Tories attribute prosperity to free markets and institutions, so this is inferred as a disagreement.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The declaration endorses a welcoming immigration system and the equality of all Canadians, which implies diversity is not seen as a threat.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Filling offices by lottery replaces the elected Parliament the declaration defends.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The declaration stresses the Charter and individual freedoms, which weigh against suspending legal protections, though security-minded members may allow exceptions.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Maximum prices conflict with the declaration's free competitive economy and the market-pricing orientation Wikipedia describes.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of media contradicts the declaration's support for freedom of expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the armed forces contradicts parliamentary government under a constitutional monarchy.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The sources do not address naturalisation waiting periods, so no Blue Tory position is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; Blue Tories favour market pay, but also public-sector pay comparable to private, so this is weakly inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The declaration asks for free votes on most matters except the budget and core initiatives, so binding discipline is limited to confidence matters.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational pooling is not endorsed; the declaration stresses Canadian jurisdiction and its free trade orientation does not require shared sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Under the constitutional monarchy the declaration affirms, command rests with the government answerable to Parliament, not with a separately chosen head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside Blue Tory politics and the sources do not address it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by senior clergy contradicts the declaration's commitment to parliamentary democracy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist wartime strategy foreign to a party that supports collective defence and a well-armed military.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship of art on moral grounds contradicts the declaration's support for freedom of speech and expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Westminster system has no term limits for prime ministers and the sources do not address presidential terms.

recall-officials.rationale: The Canadian Encyclopedia notes Reform's push for democratic reform, and recall was part of the Reform programme Blue Tories inherited.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The declaration endorses deterrence and strength through collective defence, so ending permanent alliances is rejected.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning renting contradicts the declaration's property rights and free market principles.

people-in-arms.rationale: The declaration supports a well-armed military and does not propose replacing professional forces with an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources do not take a moral view on rural versus urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources do not address divided nations, and Canadian Blue Tories have no stake in the question.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-elite populism runs through Reform and Blue Tory politics, though no source here states it for university graduates specifically.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; Blue Tories split between cultural-heritage conservatives and civic universalists.

death-penalty.rationale: The Canadian Conservative Party has not restored the death penalty and treats it as a conscience matter; adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum is provincial and the sources do not take a stand; adherents differ between libertarian and social-conservative views.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The sources do not address it; Blue Tories are not typically creationist, though a socially conservative faction exists.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Libertarian-leaning Blue Tories favour personal freedom while social conservatives favour restrictions, so adherents split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Canada's citizenship by birth is the status quo and Blue Tories do not generally seek to replace it.

minority-language-support.rationale: The declaration affirms English and French equality in federal institutions, though it does not address other minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The sources do not address religious exemptions; the declaration says there should be one law for all but protects worship.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Blue Tories stress personal freedom but also tradition; this Millian point is not addressed in the sources.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Fiscal prudence and respect for obligations lead Blue Tories to oppose cancelling debts, though the sources do not discuss it directly.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A dependency-theory claim not shared by market-oriented Blue Tories, who favour global free trade as the path to prosperity.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The declaration expects constitutional change through amendment with provincial agreement, not through a new assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The declaration lists freedom of speech, worship, assembly and association as founding principles, so suspending political freedoms for growth is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Blue Tories split on foreign aid, and the sources do not document a position beyond general accountability for public spending.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Canada relies on NATO deterrent and the declaration prefers collective defence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The declaration affirms the constitutional monarchy, so a directly elected head of state is not favoured.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Fiscal conservatism favours sound money, but the sources do not mention central banks, so this is inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Canadian Blue Tories have no documented position on land-for-peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is a fundamental right in the declaration, to be overridden only with compensation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A historical debate on the left that the sources do not touch and Blue Tories do not divide over.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The declaration favours reduced government interference and opposes carbon pricing, which implies unwillingness to regulate before scientific certainty.

collective-defense.rationale: The declaration endorses deterrence and strength through collective defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the declaration's respect for the rule of law and collective defence.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The declaration supports freedom of worship and religious freedom abroad, so curbing churches' property and power is disfavoured.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The constitutional monarchy the declaration affirms places the head of state above party politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The declaration affirms federalism and constitutional boundaries, but the sources I opened do not discuss using force against secession, so adherents' view is unknown.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The declaration recognises Quebec's distinctiveness within federalism, but does not address regions joining larger states with separate systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred or divine head of state contradicts the declaration's constitutional parliamentary democracy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The declaration asks for a less progressive tax system with fewer brackets, which moves toward a flat rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Blue Tories stress personal responsibility and self-reliance, which implies that character is not mainly circumstance; the sources do not state it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The declaration stresses ministerial accountability and the rule of law under a constitutional monarchy.

space-expansion.rationale: The sources have no position on space expansion.

mixed-constitution.rationale: A classical constitutional theory the sources do not address; the Westminster system arguably mixes monarchy, lords and commons but this is not argued.

leader-cult.rationale: Public cults of a leader are foreign to Canadian parliamentary conservatism, which stresses institutions and accountability.

equal-parenting.rationale: The sources do not address child custody presumptions.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist question outside Blue Tory thought; the idea of a socialist state is rejected.

land-redistribution.rationale: Taking large estates for redistribution contradicts the declaration's property rights with compensation for deprivation.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not address refugee return rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming territory because co-nationals live there conflicts with the declaration's emphasis on constitutional boundaries and Canadian jurisdiction.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The declaration protects freedom of worship, which excludes punishing people for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mandated dress for women contradicts the declaration's freedom of the individual and Blue Tory personal-freedom emphasis.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; Blue Tories value the Canadian dollar and sovereignty, so a shared currency is likely disfavoured.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political union of kin peoples is alien to Canadian Blue Toryism, which is federalist within Canada.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Quebec's distinctiveness is acknowledged in the declaration, but self-governing cultural institutions for minorities are not addressed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources do not address this diaspora-politics question.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis; Blue Tories attribute progress to individual initiative and free enterprise.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is accepted within a free market, but active breaking-up of economic concentrations is not a Blue Tory aim; the sources are silent.

no-bailouts.rationale: Blue Tories stress market discipline and oppose deficit spending, though the sources do not discuss bailouts specifically.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Reform/Harper Blue Tories criticised judicial activism but affirm the Charter.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Required parity conflicts with the declaration's equality of opportunity and individual-merit orientation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A closed imperial economic bloc contradicts the declaration's call to reduce trade barriers and tariffs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The declaration seeks freer trade and reduced barriers, and it opposes imposed environmental measures such as carbon pricing, so binding standards are disfavoured.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives contradicts the declaration's premise that individuals enjoy the fruits of their labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Armed vanguard action is incompatible with the declaration's commitment to the democratic process.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The declaration affirms the constitutional monarchy, which is a hereditary institution, though Blue Tories have no attachment to titles generally.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The sources do not address history curricula beyond promoting Canada's history and traditions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not addressed; a colonial-era rationale that Canadian Blue Tories would not endorse, inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The declaration commits the party to promoting Canada's history and traditions, which supports teaching national loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The declaration stresses equal individual rights and equality of opportunity.

public-money-creation.rationale: Blue Tories favour sound money and independent central banking in a market economy, not a new public money-creation scheme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Blue Tory market outlook treats a free competitive economy as durable and self-correcting.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The sources do not address cultivating influence in former imperial regions; Canada's Commonwealth ties are not discussed here.

delink-world-market.rationale: Breaking economic ties contradicts the declaration's global free and fair trading regime.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist thesis foreign to Blue Tories, who see workers sharing in prosperity through the market economy.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian sympathy exists, but the declaration affirms equality of all Canadians.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The declaration upholds the Charter and proposes a constitutional property-rights amendment, which accepts entrenched limits.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration respects constitutional boundaries and treaties, so voiding them is disfavoured by inference.

elective-rulers.rationale: The sources do not address how rulers are chosen beyond Canada's parliamentary monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Parliamentary majority rule under the Westminster system is accepted, though minority protection comes through the Charter.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources do not address a right of resistance; the constitutional tradition is neutral here.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The declaration stresses Parliament and ministerial accountability, as a Westminster conservative would.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; most conservatives accept that animal suffering matters morally.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The declaration supports farming and agriculture, including supply management, which implies acceptance of animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Canadian Encyclopedia ties communitarian duty to Red Toryism; Blue Tories emphasise self-reliance and private charity, so this is contested.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Blue Tories are active party partisans who see politics as a route to lower taxes and smaller government.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school critique not shared by market-oriented conservatives, inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis not shared by Blue Tories, inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Contradicts the declaration's view that a free and fair global trading regime is the best path to prosperity.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians.

party-own-road.rationale: Internal communist-movement debate the sources do not address; no Blue Tory position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Blue Tories value self-reliance but the sources do not address foreign aid policy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Canadian Blue Tories have no irredentist tradition.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The declaration insists on equal citizenship and equal Charter rights for Indigenous and non-Indigenous Canadians, which excludes reserved leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; Blue Tories oppose fascism but not typically as a constitutional founding value, inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not documented in the sources; Conservative governments memorialised victims of communism, which suggests agreement, but this is recalled and not verified.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historical question the sources do not address.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The declaration's commitment to promote Canada's history and traditions supports preserving monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the declaration's equality of all Canadians is consistent with agreement.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The declaration has a family-violence section but the sources do not address symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; the declaration is universalist about democracy but this exact claim is not discussed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for the military contradicts the parliamentary supremacy and civilian government the declaration endorses.

paid-care-work.rationale: The declaration supports tax relief for home caregivers rather than treating domestic work as paid labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Not directly addressed; the declaration says individuals should provide for their families, which implies family obligations.

office-by-exam.rationale: The declaration seeks an efficient professional public service but the sources do not mention examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blue Tories favour free trade and investment; the declaration wants reduced trade barriers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; Blue Tory personal-freedom views point to agreement, social conservatives to dissent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: A council-democracy idea not addressed; Reform's recall idea applies to MPs but not mandated delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Market-oriented savings vehicles such as the Harper-era TFSA suggest sympathy for individual accounts, but pensions are not addressed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Community or national ownership of land contradicts the declaration's property rights and private control of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The declaration states that ministers are accountable to Parliament, which presupposes parliamentary control of budgets and estimates.

single-official-language.rationale: The declaration states that English and French have equality of status in all federal institutions, which excludes a single official language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The sources do not address foreign ownership of land; free-investment instincts conflict with nationalist ones.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The declaration limits government to equality of opportunity, not outcomes, which weighs against treating unequal results as discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: A market-oriented Blue Tory accepts consumer choice and does not see acquiring goods as harmful.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from a preference for alliance-based, lawful action.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Troops entering an allied country without consent contradicts the declaration's respect for sovereignty and jurisdiction.

corporate-influence.rationale: Blue Tories do not regard lobbying by firms as a major problem, favouring less regulation of business, though some populists criticise insiders.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not documented in the sources; inferred from the Blue Tory critique of activist groups.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The declaration offers family tax relief but does not frame it as a pronatalist aim, so the question is open.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on who can buy property conflict with the declaration's property rights and free-market principles.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state employer of last resort contradicts the limited-government principle and the declaration's view that government should foster private initiative.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not address this theory of international relations.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The declaration upholds the rule of law and one law for all Canadians, so a lack of any duty to obey is disfavoured.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not address non-intervention in other states' affairs.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed; Blue Tories are wary of unions but have no view on craft versus industry organisation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities contradict the declaration's equality of all Canadians.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The declaration treats the family as important and discusses the definition of marriage, so abolition is disfavoured.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The declaration emphasises government accountability and whistle-blower protection, which is consistent with a right of access to information.

local-production.rationale: A localist economy contradicts the declaration's free trade principles for all sectors.

informal-organisation.rationale: An anarchist organising model that the sources do not address; Blue Tories work through parties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The declaration emphasises Canadian jurisdiction and constitutional boundaries, favouring domestic law over international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: The declaration affirms equality of all Canadians and rejects religious courts, which excludes a religiously defined nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary relations between states are foreign to Blue Tory thought; inferred from the declaration's sovereignty emphasis.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The declaration supports strong provinces and limits on federal spending power but also backs an equalization formula, so it is split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The declaration lists the right to own property as a founding principle, which covers personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not documented in the sources; inferred from a market-based worldview opposed to communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The declaration says government should provide only services that cannot be provided more efficiently by the private sector.

religion-illusion.rationale: The declaration lists freedom of worship and religious freedom, and many Blue Tories are religious, so the claim is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Blue Toryism sees a free competitive economy as the best guarantor of prosperity, which implies capitalism has been progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Blue Tories favour equality of opportunity within a free market and reject remaking the economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: The declaration supports tax relief for families caring for children at home rather than socialised care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not a Blue Tory theme and the declaration supports English and French as official languages.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from respect for the rule of law; the declaration's Indigenous section speaks of rights within the Constitution.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing cooperative communities contradict a free competitive market economy.

majority-settlement.rationale: Encouraging majority settlement in minority regions contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Blue Toryism embraces a free competitive economy, so a third way is rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources do not address historical land claims in general.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial contradicts the declaration's belief in the dignity of all human life and has no place among conservative parties.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminalising private adult conduct contradicts the declaration's freedom of the individual and Blue Tory personal-freedom emphasis.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition contradicts the declaration's commitment to democratic process and freedoms of association.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The declaration protects freedom of speech and worship and rejects religious courts.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Canada's Blue Tories have no imperial economic tradition; the free trade stance opposes colonial exploitation by inference.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A doctrine of Islamic jurisprudence outside Blue Tory thought, which rejects religiously based law.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A religious legitimacy doctrine contradicting the declaration's democratic and one-law-for-all principles.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The declaration supports Parliament and free votes, while Reform supported more direct input; the sources do not settle it.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The declaration speaks of equality and individual rights, not of overlapping group oppressions, so the framework is not endorsed.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Libertarian-minded Blue Tories favour personal freedom while social conservatives oppose, and the sources do not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: The declaration names euthanasia as an issue of conscience with free votes, acknowledging a diversity of convictions.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Blue Tories place themselves firmly on the right-wing side of the Canadian conservative spectrum, as Wikipedia describes.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist critique not shared by Blue Tories, who see employment as a mutually beneficial exchange.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The declaration affirms freedom of worship and equality of all Canadians, which weighs against declaring a religion incompatible.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The declaration grounds authority in Parliament and the democratic process rather than in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents split between secular-neutrality and religious-liberty views and the sources are silent.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a preference for freedom of contract between employers and employees.

social-market-economy.rationale: The declaration pairs a free competitive economy with access to healthcare regardless of ability to pay, but Blue Tories lean to markets.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The declaration calls for a well-armed military, so abolition is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; Blue Tories tolerate market inequality as the result of enterprise, which implies acceptance.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The declaration endorses deterrence and strength through collective defence, which implies joining Western alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Accepting the constitutional monarchy, which passes by descent, implies accepting hereditary succession of the head of state.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: User-owned banks issuing credit at cost conflict with a free competitive financial market.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Fiscal prudence and opposition to deficits lead Blue Tories to accept spending restraint.

property-franchise.rationale: Limiting the vote by property contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians and democratic process.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist thesis alien to Blue Tory thought, inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not shared by Blue Tories.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The declaration protects freedom of expression and sees private ownership of enterprise as legitimate, so the claim is rejected.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The declaration's rule-of-law and parliamentary framework favours published general laws over arbitrary decrees.

racial-franchise.rationale: Restricting the vote by race contradicts the declaration's equality of all Canadians.

online-participation.rationale: The sources do not address online deliberation, which is neither endorsed nor opposed.

open-government-data.rationale: The declaration's emphasis on government accountability and whistle-blower protection is consistent with open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The declaration lists freedom of the individual and worship as founding principles, which weigh against restricting marriage by faith.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeted boycotts of minority shops contradict the declaration's equality of all Canadians.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The declaration requires a referendum before electoral reform but does not address citizens' assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrinal reinterpretation is an internal religious matter and the sources do not address it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Blue Tories treat private wealth as a reward of enterprise rather than a threat, though concentration in the state is feared.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The declaration's equality of all Canadians and the free-vote treatment of marriage suggest acceptance, though no source states it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The declaration lists freedom of worship as a founding principle, which excludes state promotion of atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The declaration calls for more law enforcement officers, mandatory minimum sentences and tougher bail, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The sources do not address consociational power-sharing; Canada's own federal arrangements are only loosely related.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The declaration stresses personal responsibility and that government should only provide services individuals or the private sector cannot, favouring private help.

term-limits.rationale: Reform-era Blue Tories floated some reforms but the sources do not mention term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not addressed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources have no position on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Internal religious matter on which Blue Tories hold varied views; the sources do not address it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The declaration affirms equality of all Canadians, consistent with spouses sharing authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Blue Tories associate the franchise with citizenship, and the sources do not suggest extending it.

rent-control.rationale: Capping rents conflicts with the market-pricing and property-rights principles in the declaration.

abolish-ip.rationale: The declaration includes a section on patent legislation and property rights, which implies support for intellectual property protection.

uniformed-youth.rationale: State-organised drilled youth movements are foreign to Canadian conservatism, which stresses individual freedom.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The sources do not address nuclear basing; collective defence suggests flexibility.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The declaration supports collective defence but does not discuss foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not documented in the sources; inferred as consistent with the declaration's emphasis on the dignity of all human life.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Policy Declaration defends property rights and enterprise, and Blue Tories treat returns on owned and invested property as legitimate reward.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The CPC declaration supports law-abiding firearm ownership and self-protection, so a ban on all lethal self-defence is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from an outlook centred on individual liberty, markets and the present constitution rather than ancient national continuity; not discussed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the individualist, non-social-conservative stance; the sources say nothing on the construction of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the individualist stance, which resists identity-group politics; the sources do not discuss feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from restrained Canadian remembrance and a secular, market-focused outlook; the sources do not discuss sacralising the dead.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from a pragmatic, interest-and-institution view of politics centred on taxes and spending; not discussed directly.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from a civic Canadian nationalism with no diaspora-homeland doctrine; not discussed in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the focus on constitutional and market policy, not a nation-building cultural programme.

god-not-male.rationale: The big-tent party is split between social conservatives and liberals on religious language, and the sources are silent.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the party's conscience-vote, big-tent stance that leaves religion to individuals; not discussed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Blue Toryism favours free trade and open markets, and the declaration backs competition and free enterprise regardless of group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the Reform tradition of provincial devolution and civic rather than ethnic nationhood; not discussed directly.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a stated Blue Tory topic; inferred from the emphasis on individual self-reliance and free enterprise, which favours member-run unions over state or party control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Blue Toryism's free-enterprise stance, which rejects socialism and treats workers' political power as no test of a good economy.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the strand's support for privatisation and smaller government, which favours private or contracted delivery of local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Reform Party's Senate-reform tradition, which sought a reformed upper chamber as a check on the House of Commons.

municipal-property.rationale: Blue Toryism rests on private enterprise and private ownership, so community ownership of the means of production is far outside it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from its preference for market and provincial arrangements over collective, assembly-based local governance.

family-wage.rationale: Adherents are split: the market wing stresses wages set by the market, while the family-values wing backs household support, and the sources do not settle it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from its deregulatory, pro-market line, which favours fewer regulatory barriers on private medicine.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from its priority on cutting spending and the size of government, which makes large new public research programmes unlikely.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Adherents are split between free-market privacy and law-and-order concerns about untraceable money; the sources do not address it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a market-liberal strand sees no objection, while the law-and-order wing favours identification.

person-over-state.rationale: The strand's stress on individual responsibility and limited government implies that the state serves the person rather than the reverse.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Conservative declaration is a big-tent text that tolerates religion in public life, but Blue Tories are not necessarily socially conservative, so support is mild.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from Reform and Harper-era support for provincial autonomy, which treats provincial powers as secure and not as ones Ottawa may withdraw.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from its pro-market, pro-technology and pro-farmer stance; it is not a stated doctrinal position.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold no common view on urban form, and market-minded housing policy favours building in cities, but it is not an environmental claim.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Reform and its successors rejected group-based politics in favour of individual equality; inferred from that stance.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mainstream Canadian conservatism neither promotes nor condemns it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Harper-era readiness to use military force abroad and from its emphasis on a strong military.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Canadian Blue Tories accept a bilingual, multi-ethnic nation built on shared citizenship, so a common language alone does not define a nation. Inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Conservative declaration stresses equal citizenship and individual rights, which points to common electorates for all. Inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Blue Toryism has no tradition of claiming foreign plots to break up Canada; such claims would be seen as fringe. Inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Blue Tories favour lower taxes, self-reliance and cost-cutting, so they prefer students to bear costs, with aid for those in need. Inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The party opposes a carbon price on citizens and industry, so it would not accept pollution taxes as the main tool. Mostly drawn from the Policy Declaration's position on carbon pricing.

future-generations.rationale: Conservatives commonly accept stewardship of the environment for future generations, though the Blue strand stresses cost to the economy. Inferred, weak.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The strand emphasises individual rather than group-based outlooks, so it would reject weighting views by gender. Inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Blue Tories back a strong military and also fiscal restraint, so adherents are split on armament cuts. Inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The strand has no stated position on diplomatic secrecy, and governments of the type use both public and confidential channels. Inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Blue Tories champion free trade, deregulation and open investment, so state limits on capital movement run against core positions.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Blue Tories defend lawful firearm ownership and oppose tighter gun control, so a rule that only state forces may bear arms runs against the strand.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from Canadian conservatism's respect for the military and rule of law; the sources do not discuss refusal of orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the strand's preference for flexible markets and individual self-reliance over union-set terms; the sources do not address bargaining directly.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: Harper-era Conservatives used targeted tax measures for low earners, which fits Blue Tory preference for tax relief over spending programs.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Balanced budgets and limits on deficits are core to the fiscally conservative Blue Tory strand, from Manning's Reform to Klein and Harper.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from free-trade, market-first outlook that resists redistributive international rule changes; not discussed in the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Blue Tories work through parliamentary and constitutional institutions and seek to shrink government, not to destroy the state apparatus.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the free-enterprise and decentralising outlook (provincial autonomy, deregulation); not stated as a doctrine.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from opposition to carbon pricing and regulation; adherents prefer property rights and market solutions to pricing nature as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Adherents are patriotic but the strand stresses the individual over the community, so it is split on sacralising the nation; inferred from Blue versus Red Tory contrast.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the strand's emphasis on personal responsibility and cutting government spending.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Western alienation under Reform complained of central Canada's dominance, but adherents rarely use colonial language; inferred and split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the individual-rights tradition of conservatism; the sources do not discuss human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from Conservative calls to cut CBC funding and reduce government's role; not covered in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: a market-oriented conservatism with no stated view on comparative religion; its largely Christian base would not accept that all religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from its small-government, free-market emphasis: Blue Tories (Reform tradition) favour market signals over guaranteed prices, though the party defends supply management for electoral reasons.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: the strand is pro-defence and pro-NATO, so it would not support unilateral disarmament; Canada itself holds no nuclear weapons, so the question is hypothetical.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: a free-enterprise strand rejects class-based politics and unions' party ties; it is the opposite pole to the communitarian Red Tory and social-democratic traditions.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the strand's individual-rights and rule-of-law emphasis and the Conservative record of opposing harmful cultural practices; FGM is already criminal in Canada and no adherent camp opposes the ban.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equality before the law and secure individual property rights are core to the free-enterprise strand, so equal property and inheritance rights for women follow directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: the strand takes no position on linguistics, but an adherent would accept the ordinary linguistic fact that regional names do not make separate languages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: Blue Tories favour property rights and deregulation, which is sympathetic to liability, but they accept ordinary environmental regulation and the statement rules agencies out.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses individual equality and elected parliamentary government, so an official lawmaking role for unelected customary chiefs would be resisted.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The strand stresses individual self-reliance and opposes carbon pricing and environmental regulation that burden citizens and industry.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The Conservative tough-on-crime tradition under Harper favoured mandatory minimum sentences for serious and repeat offenders, though a market-liberal wing is wary of limiting judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Conservative policy stresses integration into Canadian society, and the Harper government tightened language requirements for citizenship, though the strand is not nativist.

missingStatements.text: Governments should cut personal and business tax rates to encourage investment and growth.
missingStatements.rationale: The Policy Declaration seeks broad-based personal, business and capital gains tax relief, and Wikipedia lists Harper and Harris tax cuts as Blue Tory achievements.

missingStatements.text: National governments should not impose a carbon price on citizens and industry.
missingStatements.rationale: The Policy Declaration states there should be no federally imposed carbon taxes or cap and trade systems.

notes: Blue Toryism is a faction label rather than a party; the Conservative Party is a big tent, so social issues (abortion, marriage, euthanasia) are left to free votes and answered as split. Red Tories would answer many economic items differently.
